_comment: ORDER MATTERS, AND NOT THE WAY IT LOOKS. Hotwire Native merges the
properties of every rule whose pattern matches, with LATER rules winning
(PathConfiguration#properties: `properties.merge(rule.properties) { _, new in new }`).
Patterns are unanchored regexes, so `.*` matches every path.
The catch-all therefore has to come FIRST, as the baseline that specific
rules below override. It used to sit last, which silently defeated every
modal rule in this file — lessons and /new have both been presenting as
plain pushes regardless of what they asked for.
Keep the most specific rules at the bottom.
The tab roots (/app, /app/library, /app/vocabulary) deliberately carry no
rule: the app draws a native UITabBarController (AppTabBarController) with
one navigator per tab, so those are plain default-context visits. The Create
tab's root is /app/import_requests/new instead of the bare
/app/import_requests (which has no route at all — nothing links to it),
so it relies on the 'Add a video' rule below rather than being rule-free
like the other three roots.
Adding a vocabulary word (/app/vocabulary/new) has no rule of its own and
does not want one: it is caught by the generic '/new$' modal pattern below,
which is exactly right for it — a sheet with an X, dismissed back onto the
list. Nothing under /app/vocabulary/ other than /new should ever be modal,
since a word's detail screen is a push inside the tab.
This file is served to the app by ConfigurationsController and must stay
identical to langlets-ios/langlets/langlets/Configuration/path_configuration.json,
which is the offline fallback. A test enforces it.
Authentication is a default-context replace_root flow, not a modal. There
is no useful screen behind login for a signed-out user to dismiss back to.
The native proposal handler and the rendered auth layout both hide tabs;
the layout assertion also covers server redirects whose destination was not
visible in the original native proposal.
PATTERNS ARE MATCHED AGAINST THE PATH ONLY, and that is a choice, not a
default. Hotwire Native ships matchQueryStrings = true, which matches rules
against '/app/import_requests/new?lang=es' rather than the bare path — and
every `$`-anchored pattern below then fails for any link carrying a query
string. Since the app appends ?lang= almost everywhere, that silently
demoted the modal rules to plain pushes. SceneDelegate sets
matchQueryStrings = false so the anchors mean what they look like they mean.
If you ever need to key a rule on a query parameter, that flag is why you
can't, and flipping it back breaks every anchored pattern here.
Add a video is deliberately context 'default', i.e. a plain push inside
the Create tab with the back arrow and tab bar intact. It was a medium
sheet; as a sheet it fought the iOS 26 floating tab bar and the screen
grew past the detent once a preview card rendered. It needs its own rule
to escape the '/new$' modal pattern above it — and that same rule is what
lets this path double as the Create tab's root (see the tab-roots note
above).
Review lessons are modal, matching the course lesson rule above: taking a
review lesson is one continuous session from the tap on 'Review words'
through the activities and finish page, with the tab bar hidden throughout.
The Pro paywall and its confirmation are one full-screen modal, sharing a
stack: the purchase POST navigates from /app/pro to /app/pro/success, and
both being modal keeps that inside the sheet the user opened rather than
dropping them back onto Home mid-purchase. modal_style 'full' rather than
'medium' because the plan cards, the CTA and the subscription disclosure
all have to be visible at once — a detent that scrolls the price out of
view is an App Review rejection.
